profile.summary: AttentiveFP (Attentive FP) is a graph neural network for molecular property prediction. It reads a molecule as a graph of atoms and bonds and learns a fixed-length vector for the whole molecule, a neural fingerprint, using a graph attention mechanism over node and edge features; that vector is then mapped to the property being predicted. It is a molecular architecture rather than a protein model, and it appears on this benchmark database because the DeepProtein benchmark trained it as a baseline on protein tasks.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: A molecule is represented as a graph whose nodes are atoms and whose edges are bonds. Attention layers update the node and edge embeddings, and a readout step pools the node embeddings into one vector for the molecule, which a predictor head turns into the target property. The authors report that the learned features are interpretable and that feature visualisation suggests the model picks up nonlocal intramolecular interactions from the task it was trained on. In the DeepProtein benchmark the model is configured with three AttentiveFP layers, an AttentiveFP readout and node and edge embedding dimension 64.

sections.title: Use as a benchmark baseline
sections.body: The DeepProtein benchmark trained AttentiveFP as one of its graph baselines. It does not call the authors' own code: its encoder wraps the AttentiveFPGNN and AttentiveFPReadout classes of the dgllife library, and the benchmark records DGLlife 0.3.2 in its software configuration. The benchmark also states that since its protein inputs are two dimensional, it adds edge information with edge featurisers for some graph networks. A result quoted against AttentiveFP on a protein task therefore describes a model the benchmark trained, not a checkpoint released by the AttentiveFP authors.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The official repository is a Code Ocean capsule export (licence dated 2019) with no version number and no trained weights: it ships the model code and Jupyter notebooks for drug discovery datasets. A result must therefore name the code commit and the training script used, not a checkpoint. This page read the repository at commit dda6708342ffe255ded73c459ad64214a4615542. For a protein result, name instead the benchmark library and encoder that produced it; the DeepProtein README states that its legacy graph encoders, DGL_AttentiveFP among them, are not available in its version 2 runtime.

notes: AttentiveFP is a molecular architecture, not a protein model. The record exists because the DeepProtein benchmark trained it as a graph baseline on protein tasks, using the dgllife implementation (AttentiveFPGNN and AttentiveFPReadout) rather than the authors' code. The paper (J Med Chem 2020, doi 10.1021/acs.jmedchem.9b00959) is paywalled; only the PubMed abstract was read. The authors' repository is a Code Ocean capsule export with no releases and no trained weights. A reviewer may want to decide whether this record should be marked as a baseline architecture rather than a model with a release.
